prompt:
Create a 2 minute 30 second instrumental event piece about a stellar core collapsing then expanding as light. Around 96 BPM, D minor. Begin inward and heavy: low brass drones and a slow heartbeat of skin drum used sparsely, never as a trailer loop. Collapse is compression of spectrum; the burst is a granular harmonic bloom and a high cluster, then a thin remnant. Intense but scientific, not a battle cue. Instrumental only. No vocals, no choir, no lyrics, no hummed melody-as-voice, no singing, no whispered speech. No brass fanfare, no Hollywood drum corps, no electric guitar solo.

[00:00–00:25] Low brass drone and rare skin hits, tempo felt as pressure.
[00:25–01:00] Strings grind inward; rhythm tightens; register drops.
[01:00–01:25] Sudden spectral bloom: granular noise plus high cluster, bright then hollow.
[01:25–02:00] Expansion as long distorted-string tails, no more drums.
[02:00–02:30] Thin remnant tone, almost a pulsar tick, fading.
